title: Business Ethics and Law
description: This undergraduate course is an introduction to ethical and legal frameworks currently being applied in the business environment in the United States. The course looks to engage with moral and legal challenges that businesses currently face and may face in the future, such as threats to data privacy and security, issues pertaining to climate justice and environmental sustainability, employee surveillance mediated through digitization, among others.

title: Topics in Interdisciplinary Humanities and Social Science Studies
Experiential Learning Project
description: This is an individually tailored reading course in which the student does readings and also completes an internship-type field project. The goal is to provide students with immersion in a multicultural milieu involving science and technology issues. Projects include student exchange programs, co-op placement, public service internships, community service, and other individually tailored projects subject to adviser approval. Students are expected to write up a description of their field project that integrates their field experience with the readings.

title: Topics in Interdisciplinary Humanities and Social Science Studies
Qualitative Research Writing
description: This course supports interdisciplinary humanities and social science graduate students in preparing strong proposals for external funding and providing a structured process for turning course papers into journal articles. The assignments and feedback will also support STS graduate students’ comprehensive examination process, which requires a preliminary plan for dissertation research and preparation of a publication-ready paper. STS PhD students are required to take this course in their first year. It is suggested that they take it as an elective in their second or third year as well.

title: Ethnography
description: This course focuses on methods, theories, and perspectives of ethnography, and on their applications to the various disciplines in which graduate students are working. Students will undertake original field research. Emphasis is given to foundational activities: defining a problem, research design, proposal writing, field methods, qualitative data analysis, writing ethnography, and protection of human subjects.

title: Research Methods
description: This seminar is an investigation of creative, theoretical, and historical research methods in the interdisciplinary arts. Students will be introduced to arts practice-based research discourses and will gain competence in writing and research techniques, conventions, and methods. This course is a requirement for all Arts Department doctoral students.

title: Digital Rhetoric
description: Although digital content only exists “on the computer,” it has real-world consequences. It can persuade people to change their behaviors, purchase products, vote, participate in protests. Yet, it can also deceive people and persuade them to participate in toxic activities. Why is this content so powerful, and how does it persuade people to do helpful and harmful things? Broadly, digital rhetoric analyzes and assesses these persuasive techniques and processes to understand how they make meaning.
